text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Nuclear waste reaches goal of Gorleben medium-term storage depot despite violent protests. Police cleared protesters from route to dump with water cannons and batons.
- Frankfurt Mayor Petra Roth dismisss city treasurer Tom Koenigs from the opposition Greens and replaces him with fellow Christian Democrat (CDU) Albrecht Glaser.

- German government says it is worried about the Russian parliament approval of a draft law on Wednesday claiming ownership of works of art seized from Nazi Germany during World War Two. Government spokesman says approval not in accordance with international law.

- Almost 35 years after death of 17-year-old Peter Fechter at the Berlin Wall, two former East German border guards convicted of manslaughter and handed suspended sentences of 20 and 21 months. Fechter was shot and bled to death at the Berlin Wall as his cries for help went unheeded.
- Number of asylum seekers coming to Germany continues to sink. Just 8,700 registered in February, down from 10,900 in January.
- Clear rise in equipment investment in the fourth quarter of 1996 of a real 2.5 percent, the Federal Statistics Office says.

- Only four of the fifteen European Union states -- Denmark, Ireland, Luxembourg and the Netherlands -- fulfil the Maastricht defict criterion necessary for participation in currency union, a Finance Ministry report says. The treaty requires budget deficits to be restricted to three percent of gross domestic product.
HANDELSBLATT
- Government wants to carry on with transport of nuclear waste despite mass protests.

- Head of DGB trade union federation Dieter Schulte says no longer rules out a revision of the unions' positive position on European economic and monetary union (EMU), if workers have to bear the burden of strict fiscal policies needed for fulfilment of convergence criteria.
- Strong dollar helps DAX index of leading German shares to new record of 3,355.10 points.

- Decline in constrution investment, consumption and state demand compared to previous quarter, dampen growth in fourth quarter of 1996. Central bank data showed a 0.1 percent rise in gross domestic product (GDP) from the previous quarter.

- Germany's Rheinmetall AG surprises by saying that, pending the agreement of the supervisory board of Commerzbank AG, it would buy the bank's 24.99 percent stake in car components firm Kolbenschmidt.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Blockades by protesters cannot stop transport of nuclear waste. Many injured and hundreds detained in confrontation on the route to the Gorleben dump.
- German economic growth seen stagnating at end of 1996.
- Russian parliament approves a draft law claiming ownership of works of art seized by the Red Army from Nazi Germany during World War Two.
- Former East German border guards sentenced for manslaughter of Peter Fechter.
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel says he against Munich plans for a toll motorway in Bavaria.
DIE WELT
- Nuclear waste reaches Gorleben despite resistance by 10,000 protesters. More than 100 injured.
- Former East German guards handed suspended sentence for manslaughter of Fechter.
- Ignoring the warning of the Russian government of damage to relations with the West, Russian parliament declares that works of art seized from Naz Germany belong to Russia.
